## 1. Executive summary

- **Headline MRR is not actually growing.** September MRR was **€746.1k**. October’s reported MRR is **€757.7k** — up only **+1.6%** — but that still includes customers who churned during October. Once churned customers are removed, the forward run-rate is **€732.4k**, down **-1.8%** from September.
- **October invoice revenue is inflated.** The raw October invoice total includes a **€120k annual invoice for Gringotts**, a **€5.7k professional-services invoice**, and an apparent duplicate **€19.5k Soylent invoice** with the same transaction ID from two sources.
- **Enterprise is the profit engine, but its economics are weakening.** Enterprise-plan contribution margin fell from **32.2% to 29.5%** because direct costs rose while revenue stayed flat.
- **SMB / Starter is the weakest customer economics in the pack.** Four SMB starter customers churned in October, a **26.3% MRR churn rate** for that segment, and Starter contribution per customer is only about **€0.8k/month**.
- **Paid search drove the most attributed acquisition revenue**, but **CAC payback cannot be calculated** because no channel spend data is provided.

---

## 2. Revenue & Customer Health

### MRR trend

| Plan | Sep MRR | Oct reported MRR | Oct end-period run-rate | Reported change | Run-rate change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise | €659.0k | €659.5k | €659.5k | +0.1% | +0.1% |
| Pro | €63.0k | €66.2k | €51.2k | +5.1% | -18.7% |
| Starter | €24.1k | €32.0k | €21.7k | +32.8% | -10.0% |
| **Total** | **€746.1k** | **€757.7k** | **€732.4k** | **+1.6%** | **-1.8%** |

The reported October plan numbers look healthier than the business actually is because they still include:

- **Nakatomi** — churned 19 Oct, €15k MRR
- **Slate Rock** — churned 8 Oct, €2.0k MRR
- **Mega-lo-Mart** — churned 15 Oct, €2.7k MRR
- **Dinoco** — churned 22 Oct, €2.3k MRR
- **Buy n Large** — churned 27 Oct, €3.3k MRR

Total churned October MRR: **€25.3k**.

### Segment health

- **Enterprise**: 8 active accounts, €6.78m ARR, **0 churn**. Acme’s request volume fell **-45%**, but this is consistent with the stated move to scheduled batch workloads. Excluding Acme, Enterprise-segment requests actually grew **+8.3%** in October.
- **Mid-market**: Nakatomi churned, and Soylent’s usage fell **-27%** with revenue reduced from €22k to €19.5k and several high-severity API/performance tickets. Mid-market run-rate MRR is roughly **-10%** versus September.
- **SMB**: Four of thirteen SMB customers churned in October — a **30.8% monthly logo churn rate** and **26.3% MRR churn**. Five new SMB logos added €11.1k MRR, so the segment ended roughly flat, but the churn is severe relative to its small revenue base.

---

## 3. Acquisition

### Channel performance — September + October combined

| Channel | Leads | Paid-trial conversions | Trial conv. rate | Attributed acquisition events | Attributed revenue | New logos | Expansions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Paid search | 1,420 | 102 | 7.2% | 6 | €274.8k | 2 | 4 |
| Content | 590 | 65 | 11.0% | 4 | €109.2k | 3 | 1 |
| Partner | 135 | 32 | 23.7% | 2 | €166.8k | 2 | 0 |
| Outbound | 355 | 21 | 5.9% | 3 | €80.4k | 2 | 1 |

### What can be concluded

- **Paid search** has the largest volume and the largest absolute attributed revenue. In October it was credited with €238.8k, but **€174k of that came from expansions** to existing Enterprise customers — Stark, Umbrella, and Globex — not new logos.
- **Partner** has by far the best lead-to-paid-trial conversion rate **(~24%)** and, on only two closed conversions, high average attributed revenue. But both partner conversions were in September; **there were zero partner acquisition conversions in October**, so it is still a small sample.
- **Content** is the most consistent new-logo source: 3 new logos across September and October, with stable-ish trial conversion around 10–12%.
- **Outbound** is the weakest channel on trial conversion and total attributed revenue. There is no evidence to increase outbound spend.

### What cannot be concluded

- **CAC and CAC payback cannot be calculated.** The data includes no marketing spend, cost per lead, cost per channel, or cost per trial. Therefore no channel’s return on investment can be measured.
- **Funnel conversions are paid trials, not paid customers.** Trial-to-paid
